production.note: US model years. First: Nissan's 2009 370Z brochure. Last: the latest Nissan US press kit for this car is the 2020 370Z Coupe kit, the 50th-anniversary year (nissan-us-2020-370z-press-kit); its successor is the 2023 Nissan Z (nissan-us-2023-z-press-kit). No opened Nissan page says in so many words that 2020 was the last model year.

body.note: Coupe only in this record. Nissan also sold a 370Z Roadster (mentioned in the 2013 and 2014 coupe kits, nissan-us-2013-370z-press-kit) under its own press kits; it is not included here. The NISMO is a separate variant.

displacementL.note: Nissan's US tables give litres only ('Displacement (liters) | 3.7', also in the 2015 kit, nissan-us-2015-370z-press-kit); no cc figure was found on an opened Nissan page.

aspiration.note: Inferred: the brochure describes a DOHC V6 with no turbocharger or supercharger.

fuel.note: Inferred from Nissan's description of a conventional V6.

transmission.note: '6-speed close-ratio manual transmission' and 'Optional: 7-speed automatic transmission with manual shift mode, paddle shifters and Downshift Rev Matching'. Same choice in 2020 (6MT and 7AT columns, nissan-us-2020-370z-press-kit).

powerHp.note: 370Z Coupe, 2020 model year. Quote (specifications table): "332 @ 7,000 RPM". The rating did not change over the run: 2009 brochure "332 hp @ 7,000 rpm" (nissan-us-2009-370z-brochure); 2013 "332 @ 7,000 RPM" (nissan-us-2013-370z-press-kit); 2015 "Horsepower | 332 @ 7,000 RPM" (nissan-us-2015-370z-press-kit); 2017 "332 @ 7,000 RPM" (nissan-us-2017-370z-press-kit). The 370Z NISMO (350 hp) is a separate variant.

weightLb.note: 370Z Coupe (base grade), 6-speed manual, 2020 model year. Quote (curb weight table, lbs; front / rear / total): 370Z 6MT "1,845   1,488   3,333". Same table: 370Z 7AT 3,362; Sport 6MT 3,386, 7AT 3,413; Sport Touring 7AT 3,439. Reference year is 2020 because it is the only year for which a qualifying weight was read: the 2013, 2014, 2015, 2017, 2018 and 2019 Nissan kits were truncated by the fetch tool before their weight tables, and the 2009 brochure has no weight. A 2009 figure of 3,232 lb appears only in sources that do not qualify (see discrepancies).

sources.publisher: Nissan North America (brochure hosted by auto-brochures.com)
sources.title: 2009 Nissan 370Z brochure (US)

discrepancies.reason: Model year, and source quality. Nissan's 2020 kit gives 3,333 lb for the base 6MT coupe. For 2009, the Las Vegas Sun spec block (no byline) gives "CURB WEIGHT: 3,232 pounds." and Fox News (Gary Gastelu, testing a Sport-package car) says "in a coupe that weighs 3,232 pounds it's plenty" (foxnews-2009-370z). Neither meets the weight order: not a major magazine panel, and not two independent outlets with named authors for the standard car.
discrepancies.resolution: Used Nissan's 3,333 lb with reference model year 2020.

reviewNotes: Reference year. The guide wants the earliest year with a qualifying weight; 2020 is the earliest that could be read, because Nissan's 2013-2019 kits were truncated before the weight table. If a Nissan figure for 2009 (likely 3,232 lb) can be read, the reference year should move to 2009. Also decide whether the 370Z Roadster belongs in this record as a Convertible body or in a separate record.
